column1: # Claims of the section "What you see in each mode" in docs/concepts/seats-and-sessions.md.
element
direct mode's unit, vtium@ttyN.service
seat mode's unit, vtium-seat@ttyN.service
seat mode's vtium runs as root with --vt=ttyN --no-switchvt
vtium's own session comes from the PAM file /etc/pam.d/vtium
vtium's own session has the class greeter
vtium console status leaves vtium's own greeter session out of the programs that hold a VT
in direct mode, login gets XDG_SEAT and XDG_VTNR, so the login is on seat0 and the VT
before you log in, login runs in a scope named vtium-login-ttyN-PID.scope
vtium opens seat0 at once and logs that the seat is open
vtium logs that it waits for the seat manager to give it the seat
the vtium of each VT starts without switching to its VT
logind gives vtium the seat: vtium takes its VT into graphics mode with the kernel's keyboard off, and draws
the seat taken: vtium wakes its input and displays and draws whole
Ctrl+Alt and a function key ask logind through libseat for that VT, and the shown VT's own key does nothing
logind asks for the seat back: vtium stops drawing, closes its keyboards and pointers, and lets the graphics card go
vtium tells logind it is done once its displays sleep
keyboards and pointers open through the seat manager, and log each open
vtium watches for devices on its seat
a device plugged in while another VT is shown waits for the next time vtium gets the seat
an unplugged device's read fails, and vtium logs it and closes the device
vtium console enable passes by a VT a login screen, a desktop session or another console uses now
the seat manager's connection fails: vtium logs an error and exits
